top_temples.name: Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Cave temple on a seasonal rivulet; name derives from water dripping ('tapak') onto the natural Shivlingam.

top_temples.name: Laxman Siddh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Popular pilgrimage site in Dehradun dedicated to Rama's brother Lakshmana.

top_temples.name: Prakasheshwar Temple (Shiv Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: One of the most visited Shiva shrines in Dehradun city.

top_temples.name: Santala Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Set in forested land on the edge of Dehradun, known for tranquil surroundings.

top_temples.name: Durga Mandir, Rajpur Road
top_temples.location_note: On Rajpur Road, one of Dehradun's main arterial roads.

top_temples.name: Mansa Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Bilwa Parvat; a Siddhpeeth, one of the oldest temples in Haridwar (19th century).

top_temples.name: Chandi Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Neel Parvat in the Shivalik range; one of Haridwar's most visited shrines.

top_temples.name: Maya Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: 11th-century temple, one of Haridwar's three ancient surviving temples and a Siddhpeeth/Shaktipeeth; regarded as the presiding deity of Haridwar.

top_temples.name: Daksha Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kankhal, about 4 km from central Haridwar; site of Daksha Prajapati's yagna in Hindu mythology; current structure built 1810, rebuilt 1962.

top_temples.name: Bharat Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A distinctive multi-storey temple in Haridwar featuring a relief map of India rather than a conventional deity idol.

top_temples.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: In the hills above Rishikesh; marks the spot where Shiva is said to have swallowed the poison from the Samudra Manthan, turning his throat blue.

top_temples.name: Trayambakeshwar Temple (Tera Manzil)
top_temples.location_note: A 13-storey temple visible from Lakshman Jhula, known for its striking architecture and views.

top_temples.name: Bharat Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Rishikesh's oldest temple, traditionally founded by Adi Shankaracharya; houses a Vishnu idol carved from a single Saligram stone.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Rishikesh's most-visited temples, especially busy on Tuesdays, with evening Ganga aarti.

top_temples.name: Kunjapuri Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Kunjapuri Hill above Rishikesh; one of the 51 Shaktipeeths.

top_temples.name: Chitai Golu Devta Temple
top_temples.deity: Golu Devta (regional form of Shiva/Gaur Bhairav)
top_temples.location_note: About 8 km from Almora; famous for devotees hanging bells and written wishes on the temple grounds.

top_temples.name: Kasar Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ancient hilltop shrine at about 2,116 m near Almora; noted as a site where Swami Vivekananda once meditated.

top_temples.name: Badrinath Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the four Char Dham and one of the 108 Divya Desams; the town's namesake and central shrine.

top_temples.name: Mata Murti Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 3 km from the main Badrinath temple, on the bank of the Alaknanda; a distinct, separately located shrine.

top_temples.name: Bagnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Sarayu and Gomati rivers; roots to the 7th century, current structure built 1450 by King Lakshmi Chand; the town is named after this temple.

top_temples.name: Chandika Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a hill about 2 km outside Bageshwar town.

top_temples.name: Raghunathji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Above the Alaknanda-Bhagirathi confluence; one of the 108 Divya Desams, traditionally linked to Adi Shankara.

top_temples.name: Someshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: An ancient temple just below the Raghunathji Temple, mentioned in the Kedar Khand text; a distinct shrine from the main temple.

top_temples.name: Gangotri Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the bank of the Bhagirathi River; built in the 18th century by Gorkha general Amar Singh Thapa; one of the four Char Dham.

top_temples.name: Bhairon Nath Temple, Bhaironghati
top_temples.location_note: About 9-10 km from Gangotri at Bhaironghati; Bhairav is considered the guardian deity of the Gangotri region, and pilgrims traditionally visit after Gangotri.

top_temples.name: Lakshman Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the shore of Hemkund Lake, about 100 m from Gurdwara Hemkund Sahib; unusual in that Lakshmana is worshipped alone, without Rama and Sita. This is the only genuine Hindu temple at the site -- the site's other major structure is a Sikh Gurdwara, not a Hindu temple, so only one entry is listed here rather than padding to the usual quota of two.

top_temples.name: Narsingh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Founded by Adi Shankaracharya; part of the Sapt Badri group and one of the 108 Divya Desams; winter seat of the Badrinath deity.

top_temples.name: Vasudev Temple
top_temples.location_note: An ancient, distinct temple in Joshimath separate from the Narsingh Temple.

top_temples.name: Kedarnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas and one of the four Char Dham; the town's central and namesake shrine.

top_temples.name: Bhairavnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 1.5 km from the main Kedarnath temple; considered the Kshetrapal (guardian) of Kedarnath, said to protect the valley when the main temple closes for winter. A subsidiary shrine within the Kedarnath pilgrimage circuit, listed as the second entry since it is the only other well-documented shrine distinct from the main temple.

top_temples.name: Naina Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the edge of Naini Lake; one of the 51 Shaktipeeths, current structure rebuilt in 1883 after an 1880 landslide.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Garhi
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple in Nainital, popular for sunset views over the town.

top_temples.name: Dhwaj Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Dhwaj hill, about 10 km from Pithoragarh town.

top_temples.name: Mostamanu Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 6 km from Pithoragarh town.

top_temples.name: Chamunda Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers in Rudraprayag.

top_temples.name: Koteshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 3 km from Rudraprayag, built inside a natural cave; local legend holds Shiva meditated here en route to Kedarnath.

top_temples.name: Atariya Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 2 km from Rudrapur (the district HQ) on the Rudrapur-Haldwani route; a large Navratri fair is held here.

top_temples.name: Chaiti Devi Temple (Moteshwar Mahadev)
top_temples.deity: Shiva (as Bhimshankar), with Parvati, Ganesh, Bhairav, Kali and Hanuman shrines
top_temples.location_note: About 3 km from Kashipur, within Udham Singh Nagar district though not in Rudrapur town itself; included as the district's second well-documented temple.

top_temples.name: Yamunotri Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the four Char Dham; originally built 1839, rebuilt in the 19th century; source of the Yamuna river.

top_temples.name: Divya Shila
top_temples.deity: Sacred rock/pillar shrine, worshipped as part of the Yamunotri rites
top_temples.location_note: A revered stone slab embedded at the temple wall that pilgrims worship before entering the main shrine; a subsidiary shrine within the Yamunotri complex rather than an independent temple, listed since Yamunotri is a single-shrine town.
